lead: A beam carries transverse loads. To design it, you need the internal shear force V and bending moment M at every section, not only the reactions. Cut the beam at a distance x, keep one side as a free body, and equilibrium gives V and M at the cut. Plot V against x to get the shear force diagram (SFD), and M against x to get the bending moment diagram (BMD). These diagrams locate the maximum shear and maximum moment, the values used to choose the beam section; see Unit 4 for the stresses they cause.
prereq: You need: beam types, supports and loads from 3.1, and free body diagrams with support reactions from 3.2.

sections.h3: Sign convention and the section method

blocks.text: Take x from the left end of the beam. At a cut, the left part and right part exert equal and opposite internal actions. Use one convention for the whole chapter. A bending moment is positive when it causes sagging: the beam bends concave upward and the bottom fibres are in tension. It is negative when it causes hogging: concave downward and top fibres in tension. A positive shear force on the right-hand face of a left-hand piece acts downward; it tends to rotate that piece clockwise. The opposite face carries the opposite force.

items: Take a section at distance x from a chosen end.
Keep the left part as the free body; use the right part only when it has fewer loads, and reverse the face signs.
At the cut draw V downward and M anticlockwise as the positive directions.
Apply ΣF<sub>y</sub> = 0 and ΣM = 0 about the cut, then solve for V(x) and M(x).

blocks.text: V(x) = (sum of upward forces on the kept part) − (sum of downward loads on the kept part)
blocks.where: V(x) is the shear force at section x in kN; take upward forces as positive and downward applied loads as negative in the two sums.

blocks.text: Learn the shapes first, then the end values. The table gives magnitudes; use the sign convention for the actual sign. In every case L is the span in metres, P is a point load in kN, w is a uniformly distributed load (UDL) in kN/m, and x is measured from the left end unless stated.

blocks.where: P is a point load in kN, w is a UDL in kN/m, L is span in m, a and b are distances from the two ends in m, and M<sub>max</sub> is the magnitude of the maximum bending moment in kN·m.

blocks.text: For a cantilever, a downward load always gives hogging moment, so the fixed-end moment is negative under the sagging-positive convention. Its magnitude is the sum of each load times its distance from the fixed end. For a simply supported beam, the BM is zero at both simple ends and positive between them for downward loads.
Name the two plots SFD and BMD, and label the units on both axes. These rules catch most drawing mistakes and let you sketch the diagrams before calculating every value.

items: A point load makes the SFD jump by the size of the load at that point. The BMD slope changes at the same point, so the BM curve has a kink.
A UDL makes the SFD a straight line with slope −w. The BMD is then a parabola.
BM is zero at a free end and at a simple support. At a fixed end it equals the fixed-end moment, usually hogging for a cantilever.
BM is maximum where SF is zero, or at a point load if SF crosses zero there. Check both sides of the point.
Draw the SFD first. Use its area or slope to check the BMD; see 3.5 for w = −dV/dx and V = dM/dx.

figure.caption: The SF falls linearly from 30 kN to 10 kN; the BM curve is the hogging magnitude, falling from 80 kN·m at the fixed end to zero at the free end. The true sagging-positive M is the negative of this curve.

spec.aria: Two curves along a 4 m cantilever: shear force falls in a straight line from 30 kN at the fixed end to 10 kN at the free end, while the bending moment hogging magnitude falls from 80 kN·m to zero.

examples.question: A cantilever AB is fixed at A and free at B. AB = 4 m. A UDL of 5 kN/m acts over the whole length, and a point load of 10 kN hangs at B. Draw the SFD and BMD and give the shear force and bending moment at A and at B. Use sagging moment positive.
steps: Take x from A. The UDL totals wL = 5 × 4 = 20 kN, acting at 2 m from A.
Vertical equilibrium of the whole beam: R_A = 10 + 20 = 30 kN upward.

Moment equilibrium about A: the loads give 10 × 4 + 20 × 2 = 40 + 40 = 80 kN·m clockwise. The fixed support supplies 80 kN·m anticlockwise. This is a hogging fixed-end moment, so M_A = −80 kN·m in the sagging-positive convention.
Cut at x and keep the left part. Forces are R_A = 30 kN upward, UDL 5x downward, and V at the cut. With positive V downward: 30 − 5x − V = 0, so V = 30 − 5x kN. At A, V = 30 kN; at B, V = 10 kN.

Take moments about the cut. The support moment is +80 kN·m (anticlockwise), R_A gives −30x, and the UDL gives +(5x)(x/2) = +2.5x². With positive M anticlockwise: 80 − 30x + 2.5x² + M = 0, so M = −80 + 30x − 2.5x² kN·m.
At A, x = 0: M = −80 kN·m (hogging). At B, x = 4: M = −80 + 120 − 40 = 0. The BMD is a parabola from −80 kN·m to zero; the SFD is a straight line from 30 kN to 10 kN.
examples.answer: At A: V = 30 kN and M = −80 kN·m (hogging); at B: V = 10 kN and M = 0.
examples.check:
L = 4.0
w = 5.0
P = 10.0
RA = P + w * L
MA_hog = P * L + w * L * L / 2.0
V_A = RA
V_B = RA - w * L
M_A = -MA_hog
M_B = -MA_hog + RA * L - w * L * L / 2.0
print(V_A)
print(V_B)
print(M_A)
print(M_B)

traps: Fixed-end moment sign: a downward load on a cantilever gives hogging, so M is negative if sagging is positive. Writing +PL is a common sign error.
Leaving the point load out of the moment at the fixed end. Every load on the cantilever contributes load × distance from the fixed end.
Using the UDL total at the wrong place: wL acts at the midpoint of the loaded length, not at the free end.
Forgetting that a point load at the free end is not included in the shear just left of the free end; it is the boundary load that the shear at that section carries.
Drawing the BMD as a straight line under a UDL. Under a UDL the BM is a parabola; only the SFD is straight.

quiz.q: What is the shape of the BMD for a cantilever carrying only a UDL over its whole length?
quiz.a: A parabola; the BM magnitude is w(L − x)²/2, zero at the free end and wL²/2 at the fixed end.

quiz.q: Why is the BM zero at a free end of a cantilever?
quiz.a: No material beyond the free end can exert a moment there, so the internal moment must be zero.

quiz.q: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a central point load of 12 kN. Find the maximum BM.
A cantilever 3 m long carries a UDL of 4 kN/m. Find the SF and BM at the fixed end.
A simply supported beam has a point load at midspan. At a section just left of midspan, what are the signs of V and M if sagging is positive?
quiz.a: V = +P/2 (positive downward on the left part's right face) and M is positive sagging; just right of the load V = −P/2 while M is still positive.

quiz.q: What does a jump in the SFD at a point mean?
quiz.a: A concentrated point load acts there; the SFD jumps by the size of that load.

quiz.q: A cantilever with a UDL has its fixed end at left. If you measure x from the free end, how do the SF and BM expressions change?
quiz.a: With x from the free end, V = wx (magnitude) and M = −wx²/2; at the fixed end x = L gives V = wL and M = −wL²/2.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern beam design software draws SFD and BMD automatically, but it uses the same section method and checks the diagrams against the equilibrium of the whole beam. Moving loads, such as a train over a bridge, need an envelope of maximum SF and BM at every section, not one diagram. Search for influence lines, shear force envelope and moving load analysis if you meet bridge or crane girders.
